A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Search Self-play work. All 30 pages of v1 and 33 pages of v2, including Appendices A–E, provide readable and matchable text, equations, tables, and figures.

before.justification: V1 reports original SSP training and evaluation on seven QA benchmarks, together with training-dynamics analyses and ablations in the main text and Appendix B.

after.justification: V2 retains these original experiments and adds analyses of the training answer set and proposer behavior in Figures 4 and 6.

M1.justification: The shared proposer–solver policy, RAG verification, filtering, rewards, REINFORCE/GRPO updates, and Algorithm 1 remain unchanged. Answer-set construction is newly documented rather than demonstrably modified. The ten-search-call limit added to Section 4.1 was already stated in v1 Appendix B.2.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same seven QA benchmarks using the same Wiki-2018 search environment. V2 Appendix A.4 identifies sources for the existing answer set D; it does not establish replacement or expansion of training coverage. The new proposer analyses examine the retained search-question task.

E2.justification: Table 6 removes two evaluated configurations: REINFORCE++ proposer with GRPO solver, and GRPO proposer with REINFORCE++ solver. The four REINFORCE/GRPO combinations remain, and the main benchmark comparator set in Table 1 is unchanged.

E3.justification: The new proposer analysis introduces DeepSeek-V3.2 difficulty ratings on a 1–5 scale and LDA topic-distribution analysis. Table 6 also changes the stated timing measure from training time to rollout generation time without changing retained values. The existing benchmark sampling, accuracy judge, and training configurations remain unchanged; rerunning is not established.

E4.justification: V2 substantially expands analysis of the curriculum mechanism through Appendix B.3 and Figure 6, examining normal proposer training for search usage, verification success, question difficulty, and topical diversity. Figure 4 adds answer-pool characterization. Existing solver, sampling, verification, and reward analyses remain, while the REINFORCE++ optimizer ablations are removed.

E5.justification: Figure 6c newly reports average question difficulty with a ±1 standard-deviation band, and Figure 4 includes an answer-length boxplot. Neither version specifies independent repeated-training runs or seed counts; v2 does not explain the sample count underlying the difficulty band.

E6.justification: Main benchmark scores and retained ablation values are unchanged. New supplementary findings include answer distributions, proposer validation success approaching 50%, increasing rated difficulty, and relatively stable topic proportions. Table 6 deletes the REINFORCE++–GRPO and GRPO–REINFORCE++ results, whose average accuracies were 48.1 and 29.1, respectively.

T1.justification: The MDP formulation, constrained self-play objectives, and loss and reward equations remain unchanged. Page 4 corrects policy-conditioning notation from x to q without changing the mathematical construction. No theorem, proof, or substantive derivation is added or removed.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same claims about supervision-free search self-play, proposer–solver co-evolution, RAG verification, and improvements under from-scratch and continual training. The additional appendix evidence does not redefine these central contributions.

C2.justification: Appendix B.3 newly interprets proposer diagnostics as improved information gathering, alignment with verification constraints, and increasing difficulty without topical collapse. The optimizer discussion narrows its approximately sixfold cost comparison to generation time. Existing explanations of reward hacking and the search-depth limitation remain.

D1.justification: V1 requires a predefined answer set but leaves its construction unspecified. V2 Appendix A.4 documents 50,000 randomly sampled answers from Search-R1 training data, identified as NQ/HotpotQA training sets, and ARPO training data, substantially improving disclosure of an essential training input. V2 also supplies the difficulty-evaluator prompt and changes the advertised repository from Alibaba-Quark/SSP to Qwen-Applications/SSP.

R1.justification: V2 adds citations to LDA by Blei et al., ARPO by Dong et al., and the DeepSeek-V3 technical report by Liu et al., while removing Hu's REINFORCE++ reference. Section 2 and the substantive positioning against earlier search-agent and self-play methods remain unchanged.

P1.justification: V2 makes limited abstract wording and author/affiliation edits, adds Appendix A.4 and a proposer-dynamics subsection, and renames the existing dynamics subsection to specify the solver. It also revises the optimizer discussion and adds an evaluator prompt. The main section order and most prose remain unchanged.

P2.justification: V2 adds the answer-distribution Figure 4 and four-panel proposer Figure 6. V1 Figures 4 and 5 are retained as Figures 5 and 7. Table 6 loses two rows and receives a revised caption; other changes include appendix reflow, a new prompt box, and updated first-page branding.

improvement.justification: V2 improves transparency by documenting the previously unexplained training answer pool and adds direct diagnostics supporting the proposer curriculum explanation. Clarifying rollout timing also makes the efficiency comparison more precise. These benefits outweigh the limited loss of comparison breadth from removing two REINFORCE++ rows, although the new diagnostics remain descriptive and the central benchmark evidence is unchanged.
